mateIn5.name: Mate in 5 or more
mateIn5.desc: Figure out a long mating sequence.

backRankMate.name: Back rank mate
backRankMate.desc: Checkmate the king on the home rank, when it is trapped there by its own pieces.

smotheredMate.name: Smothered mate
smotheredMate.desc: A checkmate delivered by a knight in which the mated king is unable to move because it is surrounded (or smothered) by its own pieces.

anastasiaMate.name: Anastasia's mate
anastasiaMate.desc: A knight and rook or queen team up to trap the opposing king between the side of the board and a friendly piece.

arabianMate.name: Arabian mate
arabianMate.desc: A knight and a rook team up to trap the opposing king on a corner of the board.

bodenMate.name: Boden's mate
bodenMate.desc: Two attacking bishops on criss-crossing diagonals deliver mate to a king obstructed by friendly pieces.

doubleBishopMate.name: Double bishop mate
doubleBishopMate.desc: Two attacking bishops on adjacent diagonals deliver mate to a king obstructed by friendly pieces.

dovetailMate.name: Dovetail mate
dovetailMate.desc: A queen delivers mate to an adjacent king, whose only two escape squares are obstructed by friendly pieces.

hookMate.name: Hook mate
hookMate.desc: Checkmate using a rook, knight, and pawn, where an opposing pawn blocks the king's escape.

epauletteMate.name: Epaulette mate
epauletteMate.desc: Two adjacent escape squares for a checked king are occupied by other pieces.

operaMate.name: Opera mate
operaMate.desc: Check the king with a rook and use a bishop to defend the rook.

pillsburysMate.name: Pillsbury's mate
pillsburysMate.desc: A rook delivers checkmate to the king, while a bishop helps confine it.

morphysMate.name: Morphy's mate
morphysMate.desc: A bishop delivers checkmate to the king, while a rook helps confine it.

cornerMate.name: Corner mate
cornerMate.desc: Confine the king to the corner using a rook or queen, and use a knight to deliver the checkmate.

swallowstailMate.name: Swallow's tail mate
swallowstailMate.desc: A checkmate pattern that visually resembles the appearance of a swallow’s tail, similar to a V shape.

triangleMate.name: Triangle mate
triangleMate.desc: The queen and rook, one square away from the enemy king, are on the same rank or file, separated by one square, forming a triangle.

killBoxMate.name: Kill box mate
killBoxMate.desc: A rook is next to the enemy king and supported by a queen that also blocks the king's escape squares. The rook and the queen catch the enemy king in a 3 by 3 "kill box".

vukovicMate.name: Vuković mate
vukovicMate.desc: A rook and knight team up to mate the king. The rook delivers mate while supported by a third piece, and the knight is used to block the king's escape squares.

blindSwineMate.name: Blind Swine mate
blindSwineMate.desc: Two rooks team up to mate the king in an area of 2 by 2 squares.

balestraMate.name: Balestra mate
balestraMate.desc: A bishop delivers the checkmate, while a queen blocks the remaining escape squares

fork.name: Fork
fork.desc: A move where a piece attacks two or more opposing pieces simultaneously.

pin.name: Pin
pin.desc: A tactic involving pins, where a piece is unable to move without revealing an attack on a higher value piece.

skewer.name: Skewer
skewer.desc: A motif involving a high value piece being attacked, moving out the way, and allowing a lower value piece behind it to be captured or attacked, the inverse of a pin.

discoveredAttack.name: Discovered attack
discoveredAttack.desc: Moving a piece (such as a knight), that previously blocked an attack by a long range piece (such as a rook), out of the way of that piece.

discoveredCheck.name: Discovered check
discoveredCheck.desc: Move a piece to reveal a check from a hidden attacking piece, which often leads to a decisive advantage.

doubleCheck.name: Double check
doubleCheck.desc: Checking with two pieces at once, as a result of a discovered attack where both the moving piece and the unveiled piece attack the opponent's king.

hangingPiece.name: Hanging piece
hangingPiece.desc: A tactic involving an opponent piece being undefended or insufficiently defended and free to capture.

trappedPiece.name: Trapped piece
trappedPiece.desc: A piece is unable to escape capture as it has limited moves.

sacrifice.name: Sacrifice
sacrifice.desc: A tactic involving giving up material in the short-term, to gain an advantage again after a forced sequence of moves.

capturingDefender.name: Capture the defender
capturingDefender.desc: Removing a piece that is critical to defence of another piece, allowing the now undefended piece to be captured on a following move.

exposedKing.name: Exposed king
exposedKing.desc: A tactic involving a king with few defenders around it, often leading to checkmate.

kingsideAttack.name: Kingside attack
kingsideAttack.desc: An attack of the opponent's king, after they castled on the king side.

queensideAttack.name: Queenside attack
queensideAttack.desc: An attack of the opponent's king, after they castled on the queen side.

attackingF2F7.name: Attacking f2 or f7
attackingF2F7.desc: An attack focusing on the f2 or f7 pawn, such as in the fried liver opening.

advancedPawn.name: Advanced pawn
advancedPawn.desc: One of your pawns is deep into the opponent position, maybe threatening to promote.

deflection.name: Deflection
deflection.desc: A move that distracts an opposing piece from another duty that it performs, such as guarding a key square. Sometimes also called "overloading".

attraction.name: Attraction
attraction.desc: An exchange or sacrifice encouraging or forcing an opponent piece to a square that allows a follow-up tactic.

clearance.name: Clearance
clearance.desc: A move, often with tempo, that clears a square, file or diagonal for a follow-up tactical idea.

interference.name: Interference
interference.desc: Moving a piece between two opponent pieces to leave one or both opponent pieces undefended, such as a knight on a defended square between two rooks.

intermezzo.name: Intermezzo
intermezzo.desc: Instead of playing the expected move, first interpose another move posing an immediate threat that the opponent must answer. Also known as "Zwischenzug" or "In between".

quietMove.name: Quiet move
quietMove.desc: A move that does not check, capture, or create an immediate threat to capture. Instead, it prepares a hidden and unavoidable threat for a later move.

defensiveMove.name: Defensive move
defensiveMove.desc: A precise move or sequence of moves that is needed to avoid losing material or another advantage.

xRayAttack.name: X-Ray attack
xRayAttack.desc: A piece attacks or defends a square, through an enemy piece.

zugzwang.name: Zugzwang
zugzwang.desc: The opponent is limited in the moves they can make, and all moves worsen their position.

collinearMove.name: Collinear move
collinearMove.desc: Two opposing pieces face each other, and one slides along the line of attack without capturing the enemy piece.

opening.name: Opening
opening.desc: A tactic during the first phase of the game.

middlegame.name: Middlegame
middlegame.desc: A tactic during the second phase of the game.

endgame.name: Endgame
endgame.desc: A tactic during the last phase of the game.

rookEndgame.name: Rook endgame
rookEndgame.desc: An endgame with only rooks and pawns.

bishopEndgame.name: Bishop endgame
bishopEndgame.desc: An endgame with only bishops and pawns.

knightEndgame.name: Knight endgame
knightEndgame.desc: An endgame with only knights and pawns.

queenEndgame.name: Queen endgame
queenEndgame.desc: An endgame with only queens and pawns.

queenRookEndgame.name: Queen and Rook
queenRookEndgame.desc: An endgame with only queens, rooks and pawns.

promotion.name: Promotion
promotion.desc: Promote one of your pawns to a queen, rook or minor piece.

underPromotion.name: Underpromotion
underPromotion.desc: Promotion to a knight, bishop, or rook.

castling.name: Castling
castling.desc: Bring the king to safety, and deploy the rook for attack.

enPassant.name: En passant
enPassant.desc: A tactic involving the en passant rule, where a pawn can capture an opposing pawn that has just moved next to it with its initial two-square move.

oneMove.name: One-move puzzle
oneMove.desc: A puzzle that is only one move long.

veryLong.name: Very long puzzle
veryLong.desc: Four moves or more to win.

equality.name: Equality
equality.desc: Come back from a losing position, and secure a draw or a balanced position. (eval ≤ 200cp)

advantage.name: Advantage
advantage.desc: Seize your chance to get a decisive advantage. (200cp ≤ eval ≤ 600cp)

crushing.name: Crushing
crushing.desc: Spot the opponent blunder to obtain a crushing advantage. (eval ≥ 600cp)

master.name: Master games
master.desc: Puzzles from games played by titled players.

masterVsMaster.name: Master vs Master games
masterVsMaster.desc: Puzzles from games between two titled players.

superGM.name: Super GM games
superGM.desc: Puzzles from games played by the best players in the world.
